ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The saying describes an incidental swing of the arms while already walking, used in appraisals of uncontrived Chan activity.
EvidenceBody: Tandu discusses Sansheng and Xuefeng, Caoyuan raises Baozhi and Huisi, and Baizhang Le appraises Dadian; these uses contrast spontaneous movement with conduct made self-conscious.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: The bodily casualness matters: the arms swing because one is already walking, an image later appraisers use for conduct without contrivance.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The idiom presents an incidental action performed in the course of going, often for spontaneous conduct.

ComparedThings: to swing the arms while walking
the attested dialogue, appraisal, and verse uses
DifferentThingTest.Reason: The cited masters vary the target of appraisal, but 因行 always supplies the underway circumstance and 掉臂 the incidental gesture.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: The alias renders the temporal relation between walking and the arm swing.

ModifierControls.Finding: 因行 sets the circumstance ‘while going’; dropping it would turn the phrase into an unconditioned arm gesture.

FamilyControls.Finding: General references to walking or free conduct do not qualify without the attested arm-swing image.
